Based on http://w3c-test.org/websockets/constructor/012.html I think I am correct here.

The protocol spec says

```
   6.  If the response includes a |Sec-WebSocket-Protocol| header field
       and this header field indicates the use of a subprotocol that was
       not present in the client's handshake (the server has indicated a
       subprotocol not requested by the client), the client MUST _Fail
       the WebSocket Connection_.
```

However, that is not the same as the removed text here. The removed text is when the client requested a subprotocol and the server did _not_ reply with any subprotocol.

This is tested in http://w3c-test.org/websockets/constructor/012.html

body: Maybe this should be "sequence" instead of "array"? The type system here is a little fuzzy; when this is passed on to Fetch all fetch does with it is "For each _protocol_ in _protocols_". But having it be an IDL sequence when the developer passes a JS array, and be a (JS?) array when the developer passes a JS string, is a bit strange.
Fetch PR seems good as long as you're sure CLOSING is not observable. I'll trust you and @zcorpan on that :)
To be clear, this is https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/issues/242 now.

It might actually have been observable per the previous spec, but I think that would have been a bug. This step should really have been part of WSP's opening handshake, and when that says to fail the WebSocket connection, the state in the API goes straight from CONNECTING to CLOSED, I believe. This is a somewhat weird case in that WSP considered the handshake successful, but then the API spec wants to reject the connection anyway. IIRC it's like this because this case was only identified as an issue after hybi stopped updating WSP.
